title: AI Made Human Connection More Valuable, Not Less
summary: Zach Jones, co-founder of Waffle, spent a decade in Army cyber command before building an agentic OS for non-technical businesses. Unlike most AI platforms that position themselves as faster assistants, Waffle positions AI as an operator that integrates into existing tools, and Zach still personally handles high-ticket discovery calls and cold outreach. In this conversation, we explore why automating everything disconnects you from your customer, how a three-person door brokerage saved $800K with agents, and why human connection becomes more valuable, not less, in an AI-driven world.
keyQuote: I believe that AI is going to make human connection more valuable, not less. And nobody will tell you more than a small business owner how important human relationships are because every customer is an important human relationship to them.
takeaways: Reserve 10% of your sales process for high-touch human interaction, especially with high-ticket clients. The conversion math works: referral networks still beat cold email, even if they don't scale.
Stop selling 'tools.' Frame AI as an operator that integrates into existing systems, not another SaaS login. Non-technical businesses are resistant to new tools; they respond to outcomes.
Threads and organic social are underrated channels. Zach closed six figures of deals this year from Threads posts, more ROI per hour than TikTok or LinkedIn ads.
Stay close to your customer early, even when you could automate. Cold calling a few qualified leads per day teaches you whether you're actually solving the right problem.
Specialization beats generalization. As AI handles transactional work, the future winner won't be 'the accountant'; it'll be 'the agricultural tax strategist with 15 years in the vertical.'
